memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Routine follow-up for benign prostatic hyperplasia and migraine.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports no new urinary symptoms, occasional mild headache relieved by rest.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/84 mmHg, weight 78 kg, height 1.68 m, BMI 27.6 (obese). Abdomen soft, no suprapubic tenderness. Neurologic exam normal.
IMPRESSION: BPH stable, migraine well controlled on prophylactic propranolol. Lipids borderline elevated, FBS normal, PSA 1.8 ng/mL.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current meds, advise low‑salt diet, regular walking 30 min daily, weight reduction. Return if: new dysuria, hematuria, worsening headache, visual changes, fever >39 °C, or chest pain.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Neurological examination: Cranial nerves II‑XII intact, no facial asymmetry, tongue midline. Muscle strength 5/5 bilaterally. Tone normal. Coordination (finger‑nose, heel‑shin) intact. Gait steady, Romberg negative.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: CT head (non‑contrast): No acute hemorrhage, infarct, or mass. Ventricles and sulci within normal limits. No abnormal enhancement. No evidence of chronic ischemic changes.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Follow‑up for BPH and migraine.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient notes reduced nocturia (2‑3 times/night) and fewer migraine days (≈2/month).
EXAMINATION: BP 132/80 mmHg, weight 76 kg, BMI 26.9 (overweight). Abdomen soft, prostate mildly enlarged on DRE.
IMPRESSION: BPH symptoms improved; migraine prophylaxis effective. Lipids still borderline, FBS normal, PSA risen to 2.2 ng/mL.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue meds, advise low‑fat diet, increase aerobic activity to 150 min/week. Return if: acute urinary retention, gross hematuria, severe headache unresponsive to sumatriptan, fever >39 °C, or chest pain.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Routine review visit.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports stable urinary flow, occasional mild headache relieved by naproxen.
EXAMINATION: BP 130/78 mmHg, weight 75 kg, BMI 26.5 (overweight). Abdomen soft, prostate mildly enlarged.
IMPRESSION: BPH stable; migraine controlled. Lipids: total cholesterol 195 mg/dL, LDL 110 mg/dL, HDL 40 mg/dL, TG 140 mg/dL (improved on atorvastatin). FBS 94 mg/dL. PSA 2.4 ng/mL (slow rise).
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current meds. Offer influenza vaccine; administered today 0.5 mL IM. Return if: dysuria, hematuria, worsening headache, visual disturbance, fever >39 °C, or chest pain.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Evaluation of new hematuria.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports pink urine and dysuria for 12 hours, no fever or flank pain.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/80 mmHg, weight 75 kg, BMI 26.5. Suprapubic tenderness mild. No costovertebral tenderness.
IMPRESSION: Acute hematuria likely due to BPH‑related irritation or possible urinary tract infection; need to rule out stone or malignancy.
ARRANGEMENTS: Order urine culture, urine cytology, and ultrasound KUB with post‑void residual. Refer to urology for cystoscopy. Return if: worsening pain, inability to pass urine, fever >38 °C, or clots in urine.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Referral to Dr S. K. Rao, Department of Urology, Vikram Hospital, Bengaluru.
Reason: Evaluation of painless hematuria and dysuria in a 62‑year‑old male with BPH to exclude urothelial lesion, stone, or infection.
Clinical details: PSA 2.4 ng/mL, prostate mildly enlarged on DRE, recent urine showing hematuria. Request cystoscopy and upper tract imaging if needed.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Urology report: Cystoscopy showed a small bladder stone (≈4 mm) at the bladder neck, no mucosal malignancy. Stone removed via endoscopic lithotripsy. Post‑op urine clear. Recommend continue tamsulosin for BPH, increase fluid intake, and follow‑up in 3 months.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Post‑urology procedure check.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports no urinary symptoms, normal stream, no headache.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/78 mmHg, weight 74 kg, BMI 26.2 (overweight). Abdomen soft, no suprapubic tenderness.
IMPRESSION: Hematuria resolved after bladder stone removal. BPH symptoms controlled. Migraine well controlled on prophylactic propranolol. Lipids stable on atorvastatin, FBS normal.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current meds. Advise regular hydration and low‑purine diet. Return if: dysuria, hematuria, severe headache, visual changes, fever >39 °C, or chest pain.
